name: step-ca
description: Private Certificate Authority for Unraid, providing trusted HTTPS certificates for services on your LAN and an internal ACME server for automated certificate issuance - built on Smallstep's open-source step-ca. Rather than self-signing each internal service's certificate separately (and having to trust every one of them individually), step-ca lets you run your own CA: trust its single root certificate once, and every certificate it issues - for any internal hostname - is trusted automatically. Pair it with an ACME-capable reverse proxy to issue and renew those certificates without any manual steps. step-ca can also issue SSH certificates and be used as a general-purpose X.509 CA; the ACME/TLS use case above is just the most common reason to run it on Unraid. On first start (when the appdata directory is empty), the container initializes a brand-new root and intermediate CA using the "CA Name" and "DNS Names" values below. Keep the appdata volume safe afterwards: it holds your root CA's private key, and must survive container recreation and image upgrades.

paths.name: Appdata
paths.description: Persistent CA state: root/intermediate keys, database and config. Must be empty the first time you start the container so step-ca can initialize.

ports.name: CA Port
ports.description: Port the CA listens on for HTTPS and ACME requests.

variables.name: CA Name
variables.description: Friendly name for your CA, e.g. 'Home Lab CA'. Only read during first-run initialization.

variables.name: DNS Names
variables.description: Comma-separated hostnames/IPs clients will use to reach this CA, e.g. 'ca.home.arpa,192.168.1.10'. Only read during first-run initialization.

variables.name: Enable ACME
variables.description: Enable the built-in ACME provisioner on first run, so other services can request certificates automatically (true/false). Only read during first-run initialization.

variables.name: CA Password
variables.description: Password used to encrypt the CA's private keys on first run. Leave blank to auto-generate a random password, which is printed once to the container log - check the log right after first start. Only read during first-run initialization.

variables.name: Provisioner Name
variables.description: Name of the default JWK provisioner created on first run.

variables.name: Enable SSH CA
variables.description: Enable SSH certificate authority support on first run (true/false).

variables.name: Enable Remote Management
variables.description: Enable step-ca's remote administration API on first run (true/false), so provisioners can be managed with 'step ca admin' instead of editing config files.

variables.name: Admin Subject
variables.description: Admin username created when Remote Management is enabled.
